title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VII, 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)', June 1986. This is Grothendieck's renewed attempt to found a 'tame' or stratified geometry in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse d'un programme. He does not start from point-sets. He starts from an abstract set of 'figures' carrying two order relations.

Top of page (end of a notational discussion begun on p.2):
- On p.2, a figure F read as an ordered part of a multiplicity M is written F~. Read as a set-theoretic figure in M, it is written Mulomb(F), the 'grande multi-ombre', with support Omb(F), the 'grande ombre'.
- Here he adds the parallel notation for reading F as a set-theoretic figure in the set of loci L (e.g. for a set-theoretic 'atelier'). This is written multombre(F) ('petite multi-ombre'), with support ombre(F).

Preliminary data (Données préliminaires): a triple (𝓕, ≤, ≪), where
- 𝓕 is a set of figures;
- F ≤ G means F is a sub-figure of G (inclusion);
- F ≪ G means F refines G.
Axiom At0: F ≤ G ⇒ F ≪ G. He calls it so evident that it was left out of the enumerated list. A margin note says it will be contained in At4 below.

Derived operations:
- (a) F ∨ G (or F ∪ G), the figure 'engendrée', 'réunion' or 'somme'. It is the ≤-supremum, when it exists. He asserts it is then also a ≪-supremum. Margin: the converse fails. A ≪-sup can exist, as is typically the case in the set-theoretic model Fig(L), without being a ≤-sup.
- (b) F ∧ G (or F ∩ G) = Inf^≤(F,G), the intersection figure. It always exists, even for arbitrary non-empty families. When F ∨ G also exists, it is also the ≪-infimum. Margin: the déploiement commutes with it, (F∩G)~ = F~ ∩ G~.
- (c) F·G = Inf^≪(F,G), the 'intersection fine', when it exists. Margin: it exists in the set-theoretic case Fig(L) and in the 'modéré' (tame) case.
- (d) ∅_𝓕, the empty figure, least element for both ≤ and ≪.

On the next page this becomes:
- the set 𝓜 of 'multistrates' (elementary figures, irreducible elements);
- the déploiement F~ = {X ∈ 𝓜 : X ≤ F};
- axioms At1 (all bounded-above sups exist) and At2 (every figure is the sup of its strata);
- a representation of 𝓕 as a family of down-closed subsets of the poset 𝓜, reconstructible from (𝓜, ≤, compatibility relation).

Purpose: an order-theoretic, point-free axiomatics for 'figures' in a tame geometry. Inclusion and refinement (of stratifications / multiplicities) are kept as two separate, interacting orders.
errors: The claims in (a) and (b) do not follow from At0 alone. (a) says a ≤-sup is also a ≪-sup. (b) says that when F∨G exists, F∧G is also the ≪-inf. At0 only gives the 'upper bound' half of (a) and the 'lower bound' half of (b). The minimality and maximality need compatibility axioms between ≤ and ≪, presumably the later At4–At7. As stated here they are assertions about the intended models, not consequences of the data listed so far.

The existence of Inf^≤ for every non-empty family is consistent with At1 of the next page, but only given At1. The inf is the sup of the set of lower bounds: this set is non-empty because ∅_𝓕 lies in it, and it is bounded above by any member of the family. It is not justified on this page itself.
The margin remark that a ≪-sup is typically present in Fig(L) is stated without proof and depends on the unstated precise definition of ≪ (refinement).

ideas.what: Abstract framework: a set of figures with two orders, inclusion ≤ and refinement ≪, linked by ≤ ⊂ ≪
ideas.modern_name: a poset with two compatible orders; cf. refinement of stratifications, point-free / mereological approaches to tame geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard source; tame geometry is usually formalised via o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight 1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches 'topologie modérée' without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Union / sum of figures as ≤-sup, existing only for compatible pairs; intersection as ≤-inf for arbitrary non-empty families
ideas.modern_name: bounded-complete poset / closure system (consistently complete poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard order theory (Scott domains for consistently complete posets)

ideas.what: 'Fine intersection' F·G as the infimum for the refinement order, existing in the set-theoretic and tame cases
ideas.modern_name: common refinement / meet in the refinement order of stratified sets (cf. existence of common refinements of definable stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); o-minimal cell decomposition

ideas.what: Notation multombre/ombre (small multi-shadow and its support) versus Mulomb/Omb (large) for the set-theoretic incarnations of a figure
ideas.modern_name: underlying stratified set / underlying support of an abstract figure

missed.claim: An order-theoretic axiomatisation of tame geometry was begun but never published or developed by others. 'Figures' with inclusion ≤ and refinement ≪ are primitive, and 'fine intersection' is a meet for ≪. This is a point-free alternative to o-minimality, aiming at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse.
missed.quote: F·G (=Inf^≪(F,G)) figure intersection fine (quand elle existe) : Inf pour ≪ ... Existe dans le cas ensembliste Fig(L) et dans le cas modéré
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Tame geometry is now done model-theoretically (o-minimal structures) or via stratified spaces and exit-path categories. An intrinsic two-order (inclusion/refinement) formalism could interface with posets of strata and constructible sheaves, but at this page's level it is only elementary order theory.

deep.surprise_reason: An interesting unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic 'analysis situs' with two orders. The content on this page is elementary order theory plus definitions, and the substantive axioms come later.
transcription_corrections: The axiom is labelled 'At 0' (underlined), consistent with At1–At7 on the next page, not 'Ax 0'. The margin note reads roughly 'NB. Ce sera contenu dans At4 plus bas'.
The items (a)–(d) are circled letters in the manuscript.
Parenthetical near the top: likely '(p. ex. quand il s'agit d'un atelier ensembliste)'.
The margin NB under (a) likely reads '(c'est le cas dans le cas ensembliste Fig(L))' rather than 'très le cas'.
